## Research interests

Liyi studies the security and reliability of AI agents. His current work asks how agents can:

- discover and validate real vulnerabilities;
- learn reusable knowledge through experience;
- make decisions grounded in trustworthy evidence; and
- generate and validate new knowledge beyond security.

His research spans security and reliability of AI agents, AI for security, trustworthy agent evaluation, vulnerability discovery and validation, smart-contract and Android security, and blockchain security.

Liyi believes AI will fully replace researchers in the near future and that the mission of the current generation is to make it happen.

## Students and research collaborators

### PhD students

- Ziyue Wang is Liyi's first PhD student. He formally joined the PhD program in 2026 after beginning the collaboration in 2025. Their work includes EvoHunt, TxRay, a Binance bug bounty in 2026, and A2, which found 104 real-world Android zero-days in 2025. Homepage: https://zyy0530.github.io/
- Michael Tiancheng Mai is co-supervised by Liyi. Their work focuses on finding vulnerabilities in cryptographic proofs. Scholar profile: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Wa0UF7UAAAAJ&hl=zh-CN
- Xiangwen Yang is co-supervised by Liyi. Their work focuses on AI for security and blockchain security, including a medium-severity Ethereum bug bounty awarded in 2025. Homepage: https://chnyangs.github.io/

### Honours students

- Shanshan Gao works on computer-use and mobile-use agent security and benchmark reliability. His Honours thesis, AletheiaFoundry, built an evidence-admitted benchmark and adaptive red-teaming system that confirmed policy violations in 70.9% of eligible attack runs across five mobile agents. The work also led to Can Agent Benchmarks Support Their Scores? Thesis: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1L9j00uj4bZ18_ZboLfg-COpIRTPHxzYg/view?usp=sharing
- Shane Yeow used unlearning to study how much security-benchmark performance comes from memorisation rather than genuine reasoning. His thesis exposed 22.5% score inflation in one security benchmark. Thesis: https://drive.google.com/file/d/11IAYmmny1tje7BeUu1BqZ7ky_sN-3Ipz/view?usp=sharing

### Independent collaboration

- Strick Sheng collaborates with Liyi outside a formal degree or research program. In 2026, they co-authored EvoHunt and When Agents Overtrust Environmental Evidence.
